name: Workwear Ledger
concept: An organised trade business: near-white bands, one tight grotesk, safety-yellow only where you book.
signature: inset rounded hero photo with a floating booking card that picks the service right there
price list as a clean ledger with tabular numerals and hairlines
imagery: bright, honest shop photography: chairs, clippers, real hands at work; 4:3 crops with 12px radius
why: Feels organised and dependable, and puts booking a chair one tap away on every screen.

name: After Hours
concept: The shop at night: near-black, warm copper light, a quiet serif voice and two-tone headlines.
signature: headlines where the second half fades to grey
sticky service index that lights up as the photos scroll past
imagery: low-key, warm tungsten photos of the chair, steam and blades; deep shadows
why: Gives a neighbourhood barber a premium, grown-up edge without losing the friendly voice.

name: Parchment Chair
concept: A barbershop as a literary journal: cream bands, condensed serif, quiet confidence in craft.
signature: giant condensed service names beside small price chips
section header kit with dot eyebrow, hairlines and a running counter
imagery: film-toned portraits and close crops of tools, warm and slightly grainy
why: Makes craft and tradition the story, ideal if the shop wants to feel classic rather than trendy.

name: Barber Pole Poster
concept: Loud and local: deep red poster blocks, a heavy condensed display and yellow stickers for prices.
signature: hero collage of cut-out photos and price stickers
scrolling ticker of services between sections
imagery: high-contrast cut-out portraits and tools on flat colour
why: Impossible to miss on a busy street; great if walk-ins and young customers matter most.

name: Northern Tile
concept: Swiss clarity: white page, a strict grid, one cobalt accent, everything about booking fast.
signature: oversized opening hours grid as a design element
booking slots shown as a clean tile grid
imagery: few, precise black-and-white shots on a grid
why: Clear and quick for busy regulars who just want the time, the price and the next free chair.

name: Green Room
concept: A calm, warm room: soft sage, rounded arches and an unhurried serif.
signature: arched photo frames repeated through the page
hot-towel ritual told as three calm steps
imagery: natural light, plants, wood and towels; arched crops
why: Leans into the relaxing side of a hot-towel shave for customers who want a break, not a production line.

name: Chrome and Smoke
concept: Hotel-grade grooming: slate darkness, cool steel highlights, a sharp high-contrast serif.
signature: slow push-in on a full-bleed hero image
menu of services set like a hotel spa menu
imagery: moody steel, glass and leather details, cool highlights
why: Positions the shop as the premium option in town, worth the price of a cut and beard.

name: Trade Card
concept: An old trade card brought up to date: paper tones, slab type, stamped details.
signature: stamp-style badges for walk-in hours
price list printed like a vintage trade card
imagery: warm, slightly faded photos with paper texture framing
why: Celebrates the shop's local, old-school character with a modern, readable layout.

name: Midnight Grid
concept: Precise and modern: navy night, gold accent, a geometric display face and a booking-first layout.
signature: stacked booking cards in the hero showing today's free slots
service cards with clean icon meta rows
imagery: crisp, cool-toned portraits and detail shots
why: Makes booking feel as easy as an app, which suits younger, phone-first customers.

name: Soft Lather
concept: Friendly and light: warm blush tones, a playful grotesk, rounded shapes and smiles.
signature: barbers introduced first, with relaxed portraits
rounded price chips you can tap to start booking
imagery: bright, candid photos of customers and barbers laughing
why: Warm and welcoming for families and first-timers who want a friendly place to go.
